[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Per a North Dakota governors office press release, this is an Atlas Power data center complex under construction on a 77 acre site west of Williston, North Dakota, a roughly 1.9 billion dollar multiyear investment built by FX Solutions Inc and powered by Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative. Planned capacity is staged: Phase 1 totals 240 MW across 16 buildings (350 by 30 feet each), Phase 2 expands to 500 MW, and Phase 3 to 700 MW. The release quotes Atlas Power founder and president Kevin Washington describing this as set to become the companys largest center of operations, building on an existing Atlas Power site in Butte, Montana. These figures describe planned and under construction capacity, not yet operating capacity, and critical_it_mw is left unset here rather than populated with a construction phase target.

compliance_history.event: Williams County began receiving noise complaints from residents around the site; county staff identified building code and zoning ordinance violations while responding, and determined that eight Phase 2 buildings were operating without the required Certificate of Occupancy.
The Board of County Commissioners gave Atlas Power 45 days to rectify the identified violations.

Told the May order had not been fully addressed, the Board directed Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative to disconnect power to buildings on the Phase 2 permit, under the authority of the county building code.
MWEC served a Petition for Declaratory Judgment on the county and did not comply with the disconnection directive.

The Board unanimously approved a standard 60-day Temporary Certificate of Occupancy after officials confirmed the code violations were rectified, state and county inspection requirements met, and $232,000 in fines paid. A full Certificate of Occupancy was to be considered after acoustical panels, security fencing and a required emergency access road were completed.

reading.body:
Atlas Powr Williston is a 77-acre data center campus under construction in Williams County, North Dakota, with a planned three-phase expansion to 700 MW of IT load. The operator has announced Phase 1 at 240 MW across 16 buildings, Phase 2 at 500 MW total, and Phase 3 at 700 MW total, but no operating capacity figure has been published and verified, so this site is excluded from North Dakota's state capacity tally. The investment is stated at $1.9 billion, with power supplied by Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 700 MW Phase 3 target would accommodate roughly 17,500 racks, though this is stated as a target not current reality. The workload is listed as high-density computing and cryptocurrency mining. The campus does not yet hold a full Certificate of Occupancy, though it received a 60-day temporary certificate in June 2023 after county building code violations were identified, corrected, and fined at $232,000.

North Dakota has three mapped data center facilities but publishes no operating capacity for any of them; Atlas Powr Williston would rank first by announced capacity if and when it reaches Phase 3, but that capacity remains under construction with no independent verification of power actually energized at the site.
